question.text: ‘ <math><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> ’ melts at low temperature and is a bad conductor of electricity in both liquid and solid state. <math><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi></math> is:

solution.text: Carbon tetrachloride boils at low temperatures and is a non-conductor in both solid and liquid phases. Carbon tetrachloride is made up of individual covalently bonded molecules, CCl4. Therefore, the electrons cannot flow and there are no ions. So it does not conduct in any state.
